children.game_version: A shorter circular procession game using lightweight cardboard antlers or props.

seniors.seated_version: Perform the upper body turns, arm lifts, and rhythmic steps while seated, using lightweight replica poles.
seniors.standing_version: Execute the steady walking steps without heavy antlers, maintaining a reduced range of motion.
seniors.tempo_and_range: Reduced tempo with a short, steady walking range.

movement_profile.arms_and_hands: Holding wooden poles mounted with reindeer antlers, bow and arrow, or supporting the hobby horse frame
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Circular procession followed by two opposing rows that face off, dance together, and cross over
movement_profile.partnering: Group interaction in circles and parallel rows
movement_profile.posture: Upright, bearing the weight of large mounted reindeer antlers

signature_moves.description: Dancers process around in a circle before turning and circling back.
signature_moves.name: Horn Circle

signature_moves.description: Dancers face off in two rows, dancing together and apart before crossing over and turning around.
signature_moves.name: Row Cross-Over

movement_profile.what_to_avoid: According to tradition, the historic horns must not leave the parish.

music_profile.sound_description: A steady country-dance air played on an accordion accompanied by the sharp strike of a triangle and percussion from the hobby horse's jaw, maintaining a measured, plodding pulse.

teaching.formation: Circle procession or two opposing rows
teaching.level_notes: Beginner level focusing on steady endurance and group coordination.
